dataFlow: A shopper on a sold-out product page submits their email via the storefront widget; the backend records a waitlist entry (keyed on email + item identifier) and returns an inline confirmation — duplicate submissions are no-ops. When Shopify fires an inventory-level update the backend resolves the inventory item to its variant and product, then compares aggregate available quantity to zero; if stock just crossed from zero to positive it creates a notification batch for that item, marks waiting entries as queued in signup order, and hands them to the scheduled sender. The scheduled sender (runs every few minutes) reads queued entries whose send window falls within allowed hours, sends the personalised email, records the send, and advances the queue up to the configured per-restock cap. When an order is paid the backend checks line items for variant or product external ids matching sent notifications within the 7-day attribution window and records a conversion. When a product is deleted all waitlist entries and open batches for that product are tombstoned. The merchant admin reads live waitlist depth per product, drills into individual subscribers, exports CSV, edits the email template, and configures quiet hours and batch cap.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update events for the same restock — the handler checks whether a notification batch already exists for the item where the prior stored available was zero and the incoming available is positive, and exits without creating a second batch if one already exists for that transition window.

Inventory briefly dips to zero then returns mid-batch — the per-restock notify cap ensures only front-of-queue shoppers are notified; remaining queued entries are held at status active and will be picked up by the next batch when stock returns, so no shopper receives duplicate notifications for a single restock.

Stock returns but available quantity is less than the number of waitlisted shoppers — only shoppers up to the notify cap are queued for the current batch; the rest remain active and are not skipped or removed.

A notification email fails to deliver — the send is recorded as failed with the provider reason; the scheduler does not retry automatically, and the failed send appears in the admin drill-down for the merchant to assess.

Shopper clicks unsubscribe after a batch is queued but before emails are dispatched — the unsubscribe handler sets the shopper's entries to removed and the scheduler skips any queued sends whose waitlist entry status is removed before dispatching.

Product is deleted while a notification batch is mid-queue — the products/delete handler tombstones all waitlist entries and marks the open batch as cancelled; the scheduler skips sends belonging to cancelled batches.

Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — the conversion handler performs an idempotency check on notification_send_id + order_external_id and exits without inserting a second conversions row.
